CALL TO ORDER

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Kraig Hill, Vice Chair Dennis Robert Smith, and Commissioners Jeffrey

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin. Assistant City Attorney: Adrian Fernandez, Assistant

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Mazza moved and Commissioner Jennings seconded a motion to

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recording Secretary Rebecca Evans reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONs

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION / STAFF COMMENTS

  Commissioner Mazza asked Assistant City Attorney Rusin for the procedure to
  revoke Conditional Use Permits like those used by the car shows due to flagrant
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of February 22, 2022
  Page 2 of 10

 violations.

Assistant City Attorney Rusin noted that very specific findings were required to
revoke Conditional Use Permits. If there were documented violations of the
Conditional Use Permit provisions by the property owner, the owner would enter
code enforcement and be given the opportunity to comply.

Commissioner Wetton viewed progress on the new public staircase on Point Durne
and found that the project had been shut down. He noted a new, large scar caused
by recent heavy rains and requested an update on the project’s status.

Commissioner Mazza stated the project was impacted by supply chain issues and
the supplies to build the stairs were not yet available.

Commissioner Wetton noted that the landing seemed to be at the high tide line,
which appeared to be a design error.

Vice Chair Smith asked if the landing floated with the waves or had a fixed design.

Commissioner Wetton stated that the landing was fixed but wave action came up
onto the landing at high tide. A large amount of vegetation was cleared to bring in
heavy equipment and recent rains created a crevasse. No runoff mitigation efforts
were visible.

Commissioner Mazza noted that both the runoff and landing issue questions were
raised by Councilmember Farrar at the last City Council meeting.

Chair Hill congratulated Planning Director Mollica and his wife on the birth of their
baby girl. He thanked the Planning Department for the noticed hearings list
provided to Commissioners and requested an editable version of the list in the
future, along with a list of continued items. He expressed a need for clarification
&om the Zoning Ordinance Revisions and Code Enforcement Subcommittee on the
two thirds rule as the Coastal Commission agreed with Chair Hill’s reading of the
rule in a prior instance.

Assistant City Attorney Rusin clarified that any extended discussion on the
meaning of any part of Malibu’s code would require noticing and should be
agendized for a future meeting.

Assistant Planning Director Fernandez noted that this was one of the policies
intended to go before the City Council for further direction.

Commissioner Jennings stated there was a definition in the Malibu Municipal Code
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of February 22. 2022
  Page 3 of 10

  and when the Local Implementation Plan was being written, authors attempted to
  clarify it. Unfortunately, the clarification was subject to different interpretations.
  The California Coastal Commission stated it was Malibu’sjob to interpret the Local
  Implementation Plan and determine how it applied. If cases were to be appealed to
  the California Coastal Cominission in the future, he would agree with Chair Hill’s
  point, but this should remain a local action.

  Commissioner Mazza requested clarification on the process and asked if these items
  should go to the Zoning Ordinance Revisions and Code Enforcement
  Subcommittee or if staff should omit the Subcommittee and go directly to the City
  Council.

  Assistant City Attorney Rusin noted that the Planning Commission does not have
  the authority to send items to the Zoning Ordinance Revisions and Code
  Enforcement Subcommittee. That action lies within the purview of the City
  Council. He stated the City and staff have an obligation to treat similar cases
  similarly.

MOTION  Commissioner Mazza moved and Chair Hill seconded a motion for staff to bring
  an agenda item for a presentation on the two thirds rule and application at a future
  meeting.

  The question was called and the motion carried unanimously.
